subject: Oceanography
title: Ocean Deoxygenation
description: A short lesson to help you apply Ocean Deoxygenation.

hook.text: The ocean is losing oxygen—warmer water holds less dissolved O₂, and stratification blocks resupply.

buildup.text: Oxygen has declined 2% globally since the 1960s—with larger drops in tropical and coastal waters.

discovery.text: Dead zones—areas too low in oxygen for most life—have quadrupled since 1950, now covering 245,000 km².

twist.text: Even small oxygen drops stress fish—reducing growth, reproduction, and forcing them into shrinking habitable zones.

climax.text: Combined with warming and acidification, deoxygenation forms a 'deadly trio' threatening marine ecosystems.

punchline.text: The ocean is suffocating—warming squeezes the oxygen out.

quiz.question: Why is the ocean losing oxygen?
options: Warmer water holds less dissolved oxygen
